author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have been reviewing the architecture for the new drift detection pipeline. The current plan relies on ad hoc checks, which leaves us exposed to compliance risks. I am proposing that we route all drift monitoring outputs through the compliance team for formal review. This ensures that any signal we act on meets our data protection obligations. The more rigorous the governance, the stronger our position when auditors ask how we validate model behavior. I want this integrated into the standard workflow so that every alert is signed off before it triggers an order change. This level of oversight is essential for maintaining trust in the system.
output.reclassify_reason: The author states that more rigorous governance strengthens their position and that this oversight is essential, indicating that exceeding the minimum request (ad hoc checks) with formal, integrated sign-offs would make them happier.
